words.prose: {{ar:فَ}} ({{tr:fa}}) makes the right-hand branch begin as a carried-over consequence, not as a detached new scene. Its bound position before {{ar:أَمَّا}} ({{tr:ammā}}) fuses the ayah opening with the sorting frame, so the meeting announced in 84:6 moves directly into visible classification.

topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the right-hand reception unfolds from the encounter in 84:6 rather than beginning a disconnected judgment tableau.
topics.reason: QAC identifies {{ar:فَ}} ({{tr:fa}}) as a prefixed conjunction and attachment evidence places the whole ayah inside a distributive branch, so the CRITICAL claim that the ayah boundary carries consequence from 84:6 is locally coherent.

topics.headline: bound opener fused to the sorting particle
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the very first visible segment is already tied to the following division particle, so transition and classification arrive together.

words.prose: {{ar:أَمَّا}} ({{tr:ammā}}) opens a classified case before the human slot is filled, and it holds that case structurally incomplete until the response in 84:8. Its single doubled form packages division with conditional expectation, so the listener hears classification before the person is named. The word lets right-hand receipt stand first as the sign of the branch, while the easy reckoning is delayed and the opposite branch waits until 84:10.

topics.headline: branch opened before its response
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that 84:7 is meaningful but not syntactically complete, because the favorable branch awaits its response in 84:8.
topics.reason: QAC marks {{ar:أَمَّا}} ({{tr:ammā}}) as a condition/detailing particle expecting a result, and translation support explicitly warns that the branch remains open into 84:8-9.

topics.headline: sorting frame precedes the person
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that classification is frontloaded before the human variable is named, so the verse first establishes a sorting frame and then fills it.
topics.reason: The local order places {{ar:أَمَّا}} ({{tr:ammā}}) before {{ar:مَنْ}} ({{tr:man}}), and the clause evidence supports a distributive branch rather than an unframed topic.

topics.headline: fused form holds the branch
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the single doubled particle packages division and conditional expectation in the same audible form.
topics.reason: The surface particle is a single form and the scope evidence requires a delayed answer, so the form-level and sound-level rows reinforce the same suspended branch effect.

words.prose: {{ar:مَنْ}} ({{tr:man}}) opens an unnamed human slot rather than a moral title, shifting the address from the direct confrontation of 84:6 into a third-person case. It is grammatically the subject of {{ar:أُوتِىَ}} ({{tr:ūtīya}}), yet semantically the recipient of the delivered record, so the class is defined by what reaches the person and then followed through the outcome branch.

topics.headline: unnamed human class
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the branch does not begin with rank, tribe, or moral label; the human class is created by the receiving event.
topics.reason: QAC allows relative or conditional force for {{ar:مَنْ}} ({{tr:man}}), and attachment evidence makes it the recipient subject of the passive clause, preserving the open class reading.

topics.headline: subject position with recipient force
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the grammatical tension: the person is syntactic subject but is defined by reception rather than agency.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence syntactically forces {{ar:مَنْ}} ({{tr:man}}) as subject of the passive verb, while the passive frame makes that subject the recipient of the delivered object.

topics.headline: direct address becomes observed case
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the discourse shift from direct confrontation in 84:6 to a third-person case-type in 84:7.
topics.reason: The row family depends on the local move from second-person address in 84:6 to the third-person branch pronoun in 84:7; nothing in the guardrails contradicts that discourse observation.

words.prose: {{ar:أُوتِىَ}} ({{tr:ūtīya}}) makes accountability happen to the person. The passive hides the giver and exposes the recipient, while Form IV turns the root's coming/reaching field into assigned delivery: the record is made to reach him, not fetched or authored by him. Because the verb sits inside the {{ar:أَمَّا مَنْ}} ({{tr:ammā man}}) branch, this delivered record defines the favorable case before 84:8 states the reckoning, and 84:10 later repeats the giving frame with the placement reversed. Its passive vowel shape starts the audible path toward the final right-hand phrase, allowing that placement to carry the verdict silently here before 69:19 gives such a recipient speech.

topics.headline: passive delivery exposes the recipient
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the grammar foregrounds the made-recipient and the delivered record while leaving the giver offstage.
topics.reason: QAC identifies a Form IV passive perfect, and attachment evidence fixes {{ar:مَنْ}} ({{tr:man}}) as subject with {{ar:كِتَٰبَهُۥ}} ({{tr:kitābahu}}) retained as explicit object.

topics.headline: arrival becomes assigned conferral
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the movement image that survives inside giving: the record reaches the person as imposed delivery, not as neutral arrival or self-managed attainment.
topics.reason: The local form selects Form IV passive delivery, so simple coming, request, and attainability branches are not the local sense; the root movement pressure remains useful only as the record being made to reach the recipient.

topics.headline: verb defines the case before outcome
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that receipt of the record is the branch identifier before the easy accounting is announced in 84:8.
topics.reason: The passive verb is inside the subordinate distributive branch and precedes the result clause, so the delivery scene classifies before the consequent arrives.

topics.headline: record-delivery formula
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the verb-object pairing belongs to a recurring judgment record-delivery pattern, with 84:10 confirming that placement is the contrast.
topics.reason: Contextual profiles show {{ar:ك ت ب}} ({{tr:k-t-b}}) as the top partner for this passive form, and 84:10 repeats the passive giving frame with changed placement.

topics.headline: right-hand sign speaks before speech
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that 84:7 lets the grammar and right-hand placement carry the verdict silently, whereas 69:19 gives the right-hand recipient speech.
topics.reason: The local clause contains passive giving plus the right-hand phrase but no speech, so the comparison with 69:19 survives as a contrast in how the verdict becomes visible.

topics.headline: passive form flows toward the right hand
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the passive vocalic shape and long vowel path keep the delivery moving toward the final right-hand closure.
topics.reason: The passive form is morphologically visible and the recited sequence links {{ar:أُوتِىَ}} ({{tr:ūtīya}}) with {{ar:بِيَمِينِهِۦ}} ({{tr:biyamīnihī}}), supporting a secondary sound-form payoff.

topics.headline: encounter becomes record delivery
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the abstract meeting from 84:6 becomes concrete as receipt of the personal record that enables the accounting in 84:8.
topics.reason: The verb's explicit object and following right-hand phrase make the prior encounter legible as a record-delivery scene, and 84:8 continues with passive accounting.

words.gloss_range: his book, record, written account, or fixed documentary register; locally the personal accountability record delivered to him
words.root_gloss_range: writing, written product, gathered or joined record, prescription, decree, register, and enrollment; local context selects the delivered personal record with binding evidentiary force

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: prepositional right-hand phrase that qualifies the delivery of the record

words.prose: {{ar:كِتَٰبَهُۥ}} ({{tr:kitābahu}}) names the delivered object as his own record, identified by the attached owner rather than by an article. The suffix individualizes the account, the concrete noun makes the written product stand before him as fixed evidence, and the {{ar:ك ت ب}} ({{tr:k-t-b}}) field keeps writing, gathering, and binding decree in view. The personal record is already present as evidence before any reading command such as 17:13-14, and its long-vowel cadence carries the object toward {{ar:بِيَمِينِهِۦ}} ({{tr:biyamīnihī}}). Its placement before {{ar:بِيَمِينِهِۦ}} ({{tr:biyamīnihī}}) identifies the accountability object first; 84:10 then returns the same record language while changing the mode of exposure.

topics.headline: his own record
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the object is not a generic book but the recipient's own individualized account.
topics.reason: QAC and attachment evidence both identify a singular noun with a 3ms possessive suffix whose antecedent is the branch subject, preserving the individualized-account claim.

topics.headline: record remains the delivered object
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the person becomes recipient, but the record remains the transferred object and the medium of disclosure.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence strongly licenses {{ar:كِتَٰبَهُۥ}} ({{tr:kitābahu}}) as the explicit direct object of the passive verb, so it is delivered rather than being the subject.

topics.headline: written product with binding force
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the local record carries documentary and decree pressure without turning into every possible branch of the root.
topics.reason: V4 accepts writing and prescribing/decree branches for {{ar:ك ت ب}} ({{tr:k-t-b}}), but local grammar selects the concrete delivered record, so the broader field is retained as binding documentary force.

topics.headline: gathered and inscribed dossier
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the record can be heard as a joined, stable dossier of accountability, not loose memory.
topics.reason: V4 preserves both joining and writing branches for {{ar:ك ت ب}} ({{tr:k-t-b}}); the local noun still means the delivered record, so the joining line is a limited image of gathered evidence rather than a replacement sense.

topics.headline: fixed artifact for review
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the life-account appears as a fixed written product fused to its owner, not as the act of writing still underway.
topics.reason: The local form is a concrete noun with possessive suffix, and the accepted V4 written-book branch supports a fixed product reading.

topics.headline: definite by possession, not article
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the record is identified by its owner rather than by an article, making possession the mark of definiteness.
topics.reason: The noun is construct-bound to the suffix, so the form's definiteness comes through possession while the noun itself lacks article marking.

topics.headline: recurrent record-delivery pairing
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the record belongs to a marked judgment delivery configuration, especially when joined to giving and right-side placement.
topics.reason: Contextual profiles show the giving-record pairing and the local clause joins the record to the right-hand phrase, supporting the marked configuration without inventing a new sense.

topics.headline: same record, different exposure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the personal record is already present as evidence before any reading command, and 84:10 later contrasts exposure mode rather than record possession.
topics.reason: The rows give concrete references: 17:13-14 stages personal reading, while 84:10 repeats the record language with changed placement.

topics.headline: record identified before reception mode
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the accountability object is named first and the favorable hand phrase arrives as the mode of receiving that specific account.
topics.reason: The local word order is passive verb, record object, then prepositional hand phrase, matching the structural claim that object identity precedes reception mode.

topics.headline: record carries encounter into the hand phrase
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the named record concretizes the prior encounter and is carried forward toward the right-hand phrase and its later reversal in 84:10.
topics.reason: The word stands between passive delivery and the hand phrase, giving the encounter a concrete documentary object and preparing the same-record contrast in 84:10.

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: governed right-hand noun that marks where or how the record is received

words.prose: {{ar:بِ}} ({{tr:bi}}) is the hinge from record to embodied sign. As a bound prefix, it makes the syntactic bond to {{ar:يَمِينِهِۦ}} ({{tr:yamīnihī}}) visible and audible before the hand noun can stand alone. It governs {{ar:يَمِينِهِۦ}} ({{tr:yamīnihī}}) and attaches the right-hand phrase to the receiving event, while leaving English choices such as in, by, with, or at deliberately close together: hand as place, means, and diagnostic circumstance.

topics.headline: governed circumstance of delivery
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the right hand is grammatically governed as the circumstance of receiving the record, not a loose body-part afterthought.
topics.reason: QAC marks {{ar:بِ}} ({{tr:bi}}) as a prefixed preposition and attachment evidence strongly licenses {{ar:يَمِينِهِۦ}} ({{tr:yamīnihī}}) as its governed complement.

topics.headline: in, by, with, or at remain close
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that one preposition can fuse location, means, contact, and circumstance into a single reception marker.
topics.reason: The guardrail itself flags the preposition as ambiguous between location/contact and instrument, so the polyvalent payoff survives without forcing one English preposition.

topics.headline: pivot from document to body-side
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the preposition turns the already named record into a bodily sign of how that record is received.
topics.reason: The prepositional phrase follows the record object and attaches to the receiving frame, making {{ar:بِ}} ({{tr:bi}}) the structural pivot into the right-hand sign.

topics.headline: prefix liaison binds particle and noun
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the bound preposition makes the syntactic bond to the body-side noun visible and audible.
topics.reason: The word is a prefixed preposition attached orthographically to the following noun, so the form-level liaison claim is locally supported.

words.prose: {{ar:يَمِينِهِۦ}} ({{tr:yamīnihī}}) closes the ayah on his own right hand or side. The noun is governed by {{ar:بِ}} ({{tr:bi}}) and possessed by the same recipient, so relation, side, and owner are bound in one compact phrase rather than assigned abstractly. The {{ar:ي م ن}} ({{tr:y-m-n}}) field lets physical right-sidedness carry auspicious value and rightward orientation before 84:8 announces the easy reckoning, while oath and power associations remain secondary pressure, not the selected local sense. The body-part wording compresses right-side group identity such as 56:8 into one personal receiving scene, and its closing sound chain lets written accountability and right-side placement announce the branch before any speech of joy such as 69:19. In 84:10 the same record-receiving frame answers this ending with behind-the-back exposure.

topics.headline: his own embodied sign
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the favorable sign adheres to the recipient's own body-side, not to an abstract category floating outside him.
topics.reason: QAC identifies a singular noun with 3ms suffix, and attachment evidence forces the suffix back to {{ar:مَنْ}} ({{tr:man}}), preserving the embodied ownership claim.

topics.headline: right hand bound to delivery
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the right hand is a governed circumstance of the record's reception, with place, means, and diagnostic condition packed together.
topics.reason: The noun is genitive after {{ar:بِ}} ({{tr:bi}}), and the translation support preserves ambiguity among location/contact and instrument.

topics.headline: physical right side with favorable value
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the hand remains an actual right hand while its root family makes that side prefigure favorable classification.
topics.reason: V4 accepts both right-side and blessing/good-fortune branches for {{ar:ي م ن}} ({{tr:y-m-n}}), while the local noun and prepositional frame select the physical right hand as the base sense.

topics.headline: rightward arrival, not neutral coordinate
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices a directional and auspicious orientation in the placement, even though the scene is not about the person seeking an omen.
topics.reason: Derivative rightward and blessing-seeking associations can color the favorable side, but local grammar portrays assigned reception rather than voluntary omen-seeking.

topics.headline: oath and power remain secondary pressure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices solemn authority around the right hand without replacing the concrete hand-reading.
topics.reason: V4 accepts oath and power branches for {{ar:ي م ن}} ({{tr:y-m-n}}), but QAC and attachment evidence select the governed body-side noun in this verse.

topics.headline: classification embodied, not labeled
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that right-side group identity is compressed into the personal hand-receiving scene rather than stated as a group label.
topics.reason: The supplied parallel at 56:8 names the companions of the right, while local {{ar:يَمِينِهِۦ}} ({{tr:yamīnihī}}) keeps the classification embodied as the recipient's own hand.

topics.headline: record joined to favorable side
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that written accountability and right-side placement form a marked judgment sign before any speech of joy appears.
topics.reason: The local phrase joins the delivered record to the right-hand side, and the 69:19 contrast shows that 84:7 lets the sign carry the announcement silently.

topics.headline: verse closes on the favorable sign
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah lands on the right-hand sign before the outcome is explained in 84:8.
topics.reason: The word is the verse-ending noun in the governed prepositional phrase, and the following ayah supplies the delayed favorable reckoning.

topics.headline: right hand answered by behind the back
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that 84:10 changes bodily placement, so the contrast is mode of exposure rather than receiving a record versus not receiving one.
topics.reason: The same-surah echo in 84:10 answers the right-hand phrase with behind-the-back exposure while preserving the record-receiving frame.

topics.headline: vowel chain binds giving to placement
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices an audible chain that carries passive giving into the right-hand landing point.
topics.reason: The recited sequence links {{ar:أُوتِىَ}} ({{tr:ūtīya}}), {{ar:بِ}} ({{tr:bi}}), and {{ar:يَمِينِهِۦ}} ({{tr:yamīnihī}}), supporting the secondary sound-chain claim.

topics.headline: right-hand sign anticipates easy account

topics.reason: The ayah ends before naming the account, but translation support confirms that the branch continues into 84:8 where the easy accounting is supplied.

reader_a.activated_readings_md:
1. **A written record granted into the right hand.** `ء ت ي:B002` supplies granting or bringing, `ك ت ب:B002` writing and a written book, and `ي م ن:B002` the right hand or side. The passive delivery follows the promise of encounter in 84:6. The packet gives grant, document, and hand; I infer that delivery makes the prior toil inspectable and personally receivable. The book is not an abstract verdict but a transferred object joining actor and record.

2. **A decree that enrolls its recipient.** `ك ت ب:B003` supplies a binding decree or judgment and `ك ت ب:B004` inscription into a register or group. The contrast with the book behind the back (84:10) and the two subsequent outcomes supplies classification. I infer that receiving the book does not merely communicate information but places the person within the group defined by that judgment. *Kitābahu* therefore reads simultaneously as record, binding determination, and enrollment.

3. **Right hand as blessing and rightful capacity.** Alongside the anatomical `ي م ن:B002`, `ي م ن:B001` supplies blessing and good fortune and `ي م ن:B004` the right hand as power, restraint, and the side associated with truth. The easy reckoning and joyful return in 84:8–9 supply the consequences. I infer that the location of delivery signals an enabled relation to the record: the recipient can face and bear it. The right hand is thus auspicious agency, not a coordinate alone.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: The mirrored delivery behind the back in 84:10 showed that passive “giving” does not itself determine favor; bodily relation to the record matters. The final `أَجْر` in 84:25 then clarified that the right-hand book is an enabling judgment on the way to beneficial return, not the return itself.

reader_a.activated_readings_md:
1. **A compiled record, not a merely handed object.** **Lexical evidence:** `ك ت ب` B002 is a written book, while B001 is joining one thing to another. The preceding `ك د ح` B002 supplies marks left by toil, and 84:8 repeats `ح س ب` as verb and noun. **Structural cue and role:** the book stands between accumulated toil and explicit reckoning. **Abductive move:** I infer that the document joins dispersed traces into one reviewable whole; the packet supplies the sequence but not the book’s contents. **Reading change:** `كتابه` reads as the integrated form of a life’s scattered work.

2. **Right-hand reception combines place, auspiciousness, and capacity.** **Lexical evidence:** `ي م ن` B002 is the right hand or side, B001 is blessing and good fortune, and B004 is right-hand power or rightful force. **Structural cue and role:** the placement is opposed to the book behind the back in 84:10 and is followed by easy reckoning and joyful return in 84:8–9. **Abductive move:** the packet supplies spatial polarity and outcomes; I infer that the right hand assigns an auspicious and empowered role to this reception rather than serving as neutral anatomy. **Reading change:** `بيمينه` marks a favorable capacity to receive and bear the record.

3. **A grant that arrives as binding judgment.** **Lexical evidence:** `ء ت ي` B002 is granting or bringing something to someone; `ك ت ب` B003 is an inscription functioning as decree or judgment. **Structural cue and role:** the passive grant is duplicated for the opposite recipient in 84:10, after which each placement generates a distinct sequence. **Abductive move:** I infer an issuing authority and a binding force from the passive symmetry and outcomes; neither is named in this ayah. **Reading change:** the book is received as an operative adjudication, not simply information about adjudication.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: 84:23 makes the issued book an external counterpart to the inward vessel of `و ع ي` B001/B002: both gather contents, but only the book stands openly for review. 84:25 then prevents the document/account mechanism from enclosing the favorable outcome in a fixed quantity, since the reward also activates negated `م ن ن` B005 measurement.

concept_map.definition: Harfleri çizgiyle düzenleyerek yazılı bir metin oluşturmak ve bu işlemin ürünü olan metin ya da yazılı sayfadır. Birine yazdırma, ondan yazmasını isteme ve yazmayı öğretme ise belirli yapılara bağlı uzantılardır.

facets.statement: Temel işlem, harfleri yazıyla düzenleyip bir metin oluşturmak veya var olan metni kopyalamaktır.
İşlemin ürünü, yazılmış metin veya üzerinde bu metnin bulunduğu sayfa ya da kitaptır.
Bir metni başkasına söyleyerek yazdırmak ve birinden kendisi için yazmasını istemek yapıya bağlı ettirgen ve isteme kullanımlarıdır.
Yazmayı öğretmek, yazı öğretmeni ve öğretim yeri anlamları yazı edinimi alanındaki bağlı kullanımlardır.
Öğretim yerindeki çocuklar veya onların topluluğu için kullanılan biçim, yeri değil öğrencileri gösterir.

concept_map.definition: Bir kimse, şey, görüş ya da işarette bulunan ve iyilik, bolluk ya da mutluluk getiren olumlu niteliktir. Bir kişi, nesne veya görüşten bu niteliğe bağlı olarak iyilik umma da dala bağlı kullanımdır; sağ tarafla ilgili kimi kalıplar yalnız mutluluk, iyi yazgı veya Tanrı'ya yakınlık çağrışımı taşıdıklarında bu dala girer.
